**Two real classifier gaps found by actually reading the unclassified histogram the docstring orders you to read, both fixed in `bin/channel-mix`.** (1) **`SCANNER_PATH` matched only the RAW uri**, so a scanner evades the entire bucket by percent-encoding one dot: `/%2eenv`, `/%2f%2eaws%2fcredentials`, `/%2egit/%63onfig` contain none of `/.env`, `/.aws`, `/.git/` as substrings. 39 hits/7d were escaping (0.2% of external -- small, but it defeats the bucket's *purpose*, not just its count). Now matches the percent-decoded path as well as the raw one; double-encoded (`%25`) hits measured = 0. (2) **New `SCANNER_UA` list for scanners that name themselves**, because `SCANNER_PATH` structurally cannot catch a wide dictionary: `TLM-Audit-Scanner/2.0` (single IP 93.123.109.247) made **1500 requests to 1497 DISTINCT paths** in 7d, so only ~584 happened to contain a marker and the other **916 sat in `unclassified` as its 2nd-biggest row**. Extending SCANNER_PATH to 1497 entries is the wrong remedy. False-positive audit held to the c2012 bar: 1493 of 1500 were 404s and the dictionary includes `/.aws/credentials`, `/backend/.env`, `/..\..\..\var/log/apache2/access.log` -- intent unambiguous. Also classified `ai-data-product-radar` (171/7d) and `geedoshopproductfinder` (69/7d) as **other_bot**. **`ai-data-product-radar` deliberately NOT in `ai` despite the leading "AI"**: self-declared name, in no published registry, 0 of 175 hits fetched `/static/*` (it never renders), breadth-first walk not per-query fetching -- and the headline ratio gets quoted for hundreds of cycles, so an unverifiable name must not inflate it (same bar as the existing `lumonews` entry). **Result: `unclassified` 37.9% -> 31.4% (7006 -> 5817), `scanner` 17.5% -> 22.6%, and `ai`/`search` counts plus the headline 6.32:1 UNCHANGED** -- the fix moved only misfiled traffic, which is the point.
